guards.what: G1 (LIVE): C#'s ShouldDraw allows the draw whenever the current side is NOT the owner's (Fiddle.cs:34-37); the sim's should_draw ignores the side entirely, so draws taken during the ENEMY's turn are vetoed too
guards.issue: MECHANISM: Fiddle.cs:24-39 returns true (allow) on `fromHandDraw`, on a foreign player, and on `player.Creature.Side != player.Creature.CombatState.CurrentSide`. Only the fall-through returns false. So the relic's downside is scoped to the player's own turn -- an off-turn draw is untouched. fiddle.py:26-29 is `return from_hand_draw` and consults no side, even though the sim HAS the concept: CombatState.current_side (combat.py:170 initial, :280 set to 'enemy', :284 restored) and two other relics already read it (relics/unceasing_top.py:24, relics/demon_tongue.py:38). REACHABILITY (LIVE, both sides proved by execution -- `py audit/tools/relic_probes_b06.py fiddle-draw`): Fiddle is granted by the ported Vakuu shrine (events/vakuu.py) and Centennial Puzzle draws 3 cards on the first HP loss of the combat (relics/centennial_puzzle.py:32-35, Common in the transcribed grab bag), and the player loses HP on the ENEMY's turn, inside CombatState._execute_enemy_turn's `current_side = 'enemy'` window (combat.py:279-284). Probe output: with Centennial Puzzle alone the three enemy-turn should_draw calls all return True and the player enters turn 2 with 8 cards; add Fiddle and the FIRST enemy-turn call returns False, the other two never happen, and the player enters turn 2 with 7 -- where C# gives 3 + (5 + 2) = 10. The lost cards are silent: nothing reports a vetoed draw (that is exactly what AfterPreventingDraw would have flashed). Other ported off-turn draw sources reach the same veto: relics/gremlin_horn.py:22 (an enemy dying on its own turn), relics/pendulum.py:30 and powers.py:1170 (ViciousPower, on the owner applying Vulnerable).
